facts.statement: Forcing excitatory neurons to make more SIRT6 reduced stress-induced sadness, despair, anxiety, and sleep cycle problems.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Removing SIRT6 from excitatory neurons caused depression-like behaviors and messed up normal movement rhythms even without stress.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: A specific type of excitatory neuron in the hippocampus disappeared after stress but came back when SIRT6 levels were raised.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Analysis of gene networks showed that a protein called OVOL2 controls the changes in gene activity caused by stress.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: SIRT6 physically binds to OVOL2 to keep it stable, which then turns on the production of other proteins like Nrg1.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: A drug that activates SIRT6 in a specific way produced the same stress-fighting effects seen with the genetic changes.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors suggest that targeting SIRT6 could be a new way to treat depression based on these results.
facts.subject: animals
